title: PSG given free Ligue 1 weekend before Champions League tie at Chelsea
content:
Ligue 1 has postponed Paris Saint-Germain’s league match against Nantes to allow Luis Enrique’s side “to prepare in the best possible conditions” to face Chelsea in the Champions League.

PSG were due to host Nantes on the weekend of March 14-15, ahead of the second leg of the last-16 tie against Chelsea scheduled for March 17 at Stamford Bridge.

The French league said on Saturday that the Ligue de Football Professionnel (LFP) Board of Directors had decided “with the agreement of Nantes” to postpone the match, which is now due to be played “during the week of April 20”.

European champions PSG will now have an uninterrupted period of five full days to prepare and travel for the second leg against Chelsea, after hosting Liam Rosenior’s side in the French capital on March 11.

Chelsea, meanwhile, face Newcastle United at Stamford Bridge on March 14. As a result, they will play three matches in seven days, with just two full days rest either side of their Premier League match.

Rosenior’s side avoided play-off fixtures to their calendar by finishing sixth in the Champions League league phase standings, and ensuring automatic qualification to the last 16.

PSG faced Ligue 1 rivals Monaco, winning 5-4 on aggregate.

Luis Enrique’s side were behind in the second leg until Monaco’s Mamadou Coulibaly was sent off for a second yellow card. Marquinhos and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia scored within six minutes to put PSG ahead and render Jordan Teze’s late goal a consolation.
